messages:
incident-bot: Paging @oncall (priority: P1) — KV cache memory blowup across a subset of runtime pods in us-west-2. Multiple worker OOMs and CUDA malloc failures observed. Triggered at 03:13 UTC. Please respond.
oncall-bot: @emma you are on-call for this rotation — please ack and start triage. :pager:
emma: acked. jumping in. seeing repeated `cudaMalloc` failures + high fragmentation metric on kv_cache_arena.
raj: I can help. Which service? runtime-prod-gpu-3 cluster, mostly models serving continuous-batching workloads (chat) — spike in batch size and cache slots.
lucas: corroborating logs: lots of `Failed to allocate 128MB` from torch, followed by worker restart loop. Metrics: kv_cache_slots_in_use doubled in 2m; kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio rose from 12% -> 68%.
emma: initial mitigation idea: throttle continuous batching + lower max_tokens_per_batch to reduce immediate pressure. Can someone push config to canary?
sylvia: I'll apply a safe canary to the canary pool now: PATCH /config -> {"continuous_batching.enabled":false, "max_tokens_per_batch":512} (rollout 10% immediate).
ops-runner-bot: Deploy started: config-canary-2026-03-15T03:16Z. Canary target: runtime-prod-gpu-3-a,b.
emma: while canary rolls, check CUDA allocator env: what is PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF on affected pods? jordan-ml: my read — it's unset in prod. That may be making fragmentation worse.
raj: quick mitigation we can do without restarts: enable larger max_split_size_mb via env and trigger a graceful restart of the canary workers. Proposed: export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128 then restart.
lucas: also propose running an arena compaction pass in-process: we have endpoint /admin/kv/compact that will try to free unused arena slabs — low-risk, nonblocking.
emma: run both on canary: set env + compact. sylvia, please coordinate the restart window.
sylvia: done. applied env + compact to canary. Restarting 2 canary workers. Logs: `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF set`, `kv_arena_compact OK`, workers back up.
ops-runner-bot: Canary health: cpu/gpu/latency stable, OOM count for canary reduced to 0 over 2m.
emma: canary looks good. Rolling to 50% while we monitor.
mike-sre: note: customers with long-moving contexts may still have elevated slots; I recommend a background compaction sweep on older hosts and a temporary change to KV_CACHE_MAX_SLOTS_PER_SESSION from 4096 -> 2048. That reduces per-request slot retention.
jordan-ml: agree. Also we should enforce a short-lived global throttling rule: reduce continuous batch window from 200ms -> 50ms to avoid batch accumulation hitting compaction backlog.
lucas: executing background compaction script across non-canary hosts now (parallel, rate-limited). Running: `for host in ...; curl -XPOST http://$host/admin/kv/compact` output: many freed slabs, fragmentation ratio dropping ~15-25% per host.
raj: pushing KV_CACHE_MAX_SLOTS_PER_SESSION -> 2048 cluster-wide via runtime-config-service. This does not require node restart. Policy rollout begun.
emma: customer-impact check: which customers saw errors/timeouts? I pulled traces — ~2.3% of requests returned 5xx in the 03:12-03:22 window, mostly timeouts from large chat sessions. No major SLA breaches yet but repeat errors for 3 enterprise tenants (tenant-A, tenant-C, tenant-E) — CS notified.
sylvia: escalation: opened incident ticket INC-2026-0315-09 and emailed account reps for tenant-A/C/E.
mike-sre: monitoring: added alert for `kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio > 50%` and `cuda_malloc_fail_rate > 0.5/min` to catch recurrence.
emma: current status: continuous batching temporarily disabled on 100% of GPUs, max_tokens_per_batch lowered, PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF set to max_split_size_mb:128, KV_CACHE_MAX_SLOTS_PER_SESSION lowered, background compaction run on all hosts. Observed: OOMs stopped, fragmentation ratio trending down from 68% -> 24% over 12m.
jordan-ml: root-cause hypothesis: a recent continuous-batching heuristic change allowed extremely long prefix reuse and increased kv slot retention per session combined with default CUDA allocator behavior, causing slab fragmentation and inability to satisfy large contiguous allocations.
lucas: follow-up actions: revert heuristic change in next patch, add unit/regression test that simulates long-prefix sessions and tracks fragmentation, and tune default PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF for prod images.
raj: ops follow-ups: add a fast-path in runtime to evict least-recently-used session slots when fragmentation crosses threshold, and throttle batch growth when kv_arena_utilization > 70%.
emma: customer comms: CS to send short update: issue mitigated, no data loss, elevated error window 03:12-03:22 affecting small % of traffic, we will follow up with RCA and timeline.
sylvia: oncall handoff: @mike-sre you take post-mortem lead for next 12h, I'll compile timelines + deploy logs.
mike-sre: taking handoff. I'll open postmortem doc and schedule follow-up. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident marked as mitigated at 03:25 UTC. Follow-up required: RCA + tests + config defaults.
